source.title: Training instabilities favor flatter solutions in gradient descent

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper text; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extracting the relevant results.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether training conditions affect held-out performance and curvature, using learning-rate sweeps and curvature measurements. Its results do not test the specific behaviors named in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The paper reports learning-rate and optimizer results relevant to the broader claim, but none directly test a listed version. Theoretical results and cited prior work are not recorded as empirical rows. Figure-only values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study's own results concern learning-rate instabilities, unnormalized Hessian curvature, and preconditioner clipping. None tests V1–V8: it does not measure magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, compare adaptive optimizers against SGD under V4's conditions, or compare batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors attribute improved generalization to instability-driven eigenvector rotations and accumulated flattening, report persistence under SGD, and propose Clipped-Ada to restore beneficial instabilities in adaptive optimization. These conclusions concern their curvature framework, not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies learning rates to induce or suppress training instabilities and measures validation performance and curvature; it does not use the original studies' methods for the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate, duration of the initial large-learning-rate phase, dataset and architecture, controlled SGD noise scale, and Clipped-Ada clipping threshold affect reported outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: VGG19 validation accuracy rises from 67.1% to 73.6% on CIFAR10-50k and from 78.1% to 84.1% with static augmentation as learning rate increases from 0.1 to 3.2; augmented ResNet20 rises from 83.7% to 87.3%. The unaugmented VGG19 sequence is not monotonic.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger learning rates can improve held-out accuracy in deterministic image-classification training within a range below divergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 6.3 reports approximately flat validation accuracy below the stability threshold, improvements within the unstable regime, and degradation at excessively large learning rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate instability can improve generalization within a task-dependent beneficial range.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing learning rate improves generalization even at constant predicted diffusion temperature; longer initial large-learning-rate SGD phases improve accuracy. Pure GD and SGD can reach similar Hessian sharpness while having different accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Diffusion temperature and unnormalized terminal Hessian sharpness alone do not fully explain these generalization results.

fits_no_version.finding: Clipping adaptive second-moment estimates improves VGG validation accuracy in the reported full-batch and minibatch experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Restoring instabilities through preconditioner clipping can improve adaptive-optimizer generalization in these settings.

record.problems: The authors note that theoretical derivations are restricted to MLPs and empirical validation relies on finite-sample estimates of higher-order curvature moments. Main deterministic experiments use reduced datasets, with only selected results benchmarked on full CIFAR10. The paper excludes divergent trajectories from metric correlations. Several generalization sweeps are presented only in figures without transcribed values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible claim-version results were omitted. Theoretical statements, cited results from prior work, and figure values not described in the text were not converted into numeric rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, corresponding natural-label generalization, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Matched convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparisons and the roles of local connectivity and initialization.
Adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance under limited or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching optimizers.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes that remove those effects.
Adding or removing dropout, small-data and excessive-dropout regimes, and interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its ranking of generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally sized random removals and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; this does not dispute the reported learning-rate effects. No eligible version-specific results are missing. The record's code-release field is incorrect: the introduction and Appendix K explicitly state that code is available. Section 6.2 describes completion at greater than 99.99% training accuracy, while Appendix K.3 additionally describes post-hoc validation-loss stopping; this qualification matters when interpreting matched optimization endpoints.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence; random-label test performance.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization under the specified comparisons.
Whether adaptive optimizers generalize worse than SGD under limited tuning, and the specified tuning or recovery conditions.
The effect of batch size under fixed epoch budgets and the specified recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbation sharpness as a ranking measure of train–test gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: VGGs
rows.operation_detail: Trained with large-learning-rate SGD, then switched to low-learning-rate GD at different training stages.
rows.value: Large-η SGD consistently generalizes better; longer exposure yields flatter minima and higher test accuracy; full-SGD performs best
rows.note: The text reports the directional outcome; exact plotted values are not given in the supplied text.
rows.check: Combines final sharpness and accuracy, which should be separate measures. Sharpness is unnormalized Hessian curvature, not V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure; epoch budgets are not matched for V5.

rows.subject: RMSprop
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated Clipped-Ada clipping thresholds and learning rates on CIFAR10-5k.
rows.baseline: Loose clipping behaves like standard adaptive optimization
rows.value: Tighter clipping restores instabilities and improves validation accuracy; large learning rates and moderate clipping give best out-of-sample performance
rows.note: This is a result for the paper's Clipped-Ada method, not a comparison of adaptive optimizers under the tuning conditions in V4.
rows.check: Subject should be VGG networks trained with RMSprop-based Clipped-Ada, not RMSprop as a model. This is the paper's method comparison against loose clipping, without V4's adaptive-versus-SGD comparison.
